title: Map Building & SLAM Configuration
contentStatus: Draft for DiFacto review. Title and content to be confirmed.

sections.title: From Understanding SLAM to Configuring It
learningObjectives: Understand the Programmer's active role in the mapping process
sections.content: L1-M2 explained SLAM conceptually - localization and mapping happening together. As a Programmer, you actively perform this process: guiding MoRo through a new space to build its initial map, a core task that comes together in the capstone commissioning module (L3B-M6). This module covers the principles behind it.

keyTerms.note: The process of determining position while building a map of the surrounding environment — covered in L1-M2.

sections.title: Preparing for a Mapping Pass
learningObjectives: Understand what preparation improves map quality
Recognize environmental factors that affect mapping
sections.content: Before starting a mapping pass, the space should be in a representative state - typical equipment positions, no unusual temporary obstructions that won't normally be present during operation. Mapping during representative conditions produces a map that reflects actual operational reality, rather than an idealized or atypical snapshot of the space.

video.title: A good mapping pass in 30 seconds
video.transcript: A good mapping pass, in 30 seconds. Map the space as it normally is. Typical equipment positions, no unusual obstructions. Guide MoRo through the space methodically. Cover every area it will need to navigate. Go at a deliberate pace, not a rushed one. LiDAR then builds an accurate picture as it goes.

sections.title: Performing the Mapping Pass
learningObjectives: Know that mapping guides MoRo through the space methodically, covering every area, at a deliberate pace
sections.content: During mapping, MoRo is guided through the space methodically, ensuring full coverage of areas it will need to navigate operationally. Moving at a deliberate pace, rather than rushing, allows LiDAR to build an accurate picture as it goes. Specific guided-mapping procedure within ANT Server will be confirmed against DiFacto's documentation.

keyTerms.note: The server-side component of MoRo's ANT platform, used here for guided mapping procedures.
A sensor that measures distance by timing reflected laser light, used by MoRo to see its surroundings.

sections.title: Reviewing and Validating a Map
learningObjectives: Understand what reviewing a completed map involves
Know what issues to look for before considering a map finalized
sections.content: After a mapping pass, the resulting map should be reviewed before being put into operational use - checking for gaps in coverage, unexpected artifacts, or areas that look inconsistent with the actual space. Catching mapping issues at this stage is far easier than discovering them later through operational problems once missions are already running against a flawed map.

keyTerms.note: An unexpected or false feature in a map that does not match the real space.

sections.title: Updating an Existing Map
learningObjectives: Know when an existing map needs updating
Recognize the difference between a full remapping and a partial update
sections.content: When a facility layout changes - new equipment, relocated obstacles - the existing map needs updating rather than necessarily starting over completely. Depending on the scope of change, this might mean a full remapping pass or a more targeted update covering just the changed area. Specific update procedures will be confirmed against DiFacto's operational guidance.

sections.title: Multi-Floor and Multi-Zone Considerations
learningObjectives: Understand the general concept of managing multiple distinct map areas
Recognize this as context for larger or more complex deployments
sections.content: Larger facilities may require separate maps for different floors or distinct operational zones, rather than one continuous map. This module introduces the concept; detailed multi-zone configuration becomes more relevant as deployments scale, connecting to the broader architecture considerations covered later in L4A.

questions.question: On mapping day, pallets are stacked in an aisle that is normally clear. What does the lesson say about mapping now?
options: The pallets make no difference to the map
The space is not in a representative state, so the map would be an atypical snapshot
questions.feedback: Correct. Mapping during typical conditions produces a map that matches real operational use.

questions.question: Why does the lesson recommend a deliberate pace during a mapping pass?
options: It replaces the map review afterward
It lets LiDAR build an accurate picture as MoRo goes
questions.feedback: Correct. A deliberate pace supports an accurate picture as MoRo moves through the space.

questions.question: Which finding in a map review is a reason to hold the map back from operational use?
options: The mapping pass took longer than planned
An area looks inconsistent with the actual space
The map was built in typical conditions
questions.feedback: Correct. Reviewing a map catches gaps or artifacts before they cause operational problems.

questions.question: When a facility layout changes, is a full remapping always required?
options: Not necessarily - a targeted update may suffice depending on the scope of change
Maps never need updating once created
Yes, a full remap is always required, regardless of how small the layout change is
questions.feedback: Correct. The appropriate update approach depends on how much actually changed.

questions.question: What does the lesson say about maps in larger facilities?
options: One continuous map is always required
Separate maps may be needed for different floors or distinct operational zones
Each mission needs its own map
questions.feedback: Correct. Larger or more complex facilities may require multi-zone or multi-floor map management.
